newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Dole clash over Mideast, Bosnia, Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Dole clash over Mideast, Bosnia, Cuba.

text.p: President Bill Clinton defended his handling of foreign policy on Sunday night, but Republican rival Bob Dole said Clinton had sent more U.S. troops abroad than any other president in history.

In their first presidential debate, which was televised live, Dole aggressively challenged Clinton's handling of foreign affairs. "He's deployed more troops than any president in history around the world," Dole said, complaining of U.S. commitments to U.N. peacekeeping efforts.
Dole, asked about Clinton's sponsoring of a Mideast peace summit in Washington last week, said he was "disappointed" that the president had not called for an unconditional end to the violence there.
"It's almost like an ad hoc foreign policy ... Get up in the morning, read the papers, see what country's in trouble, say let's have a meeting," Dole said. "I think we have lost credibility."

Clinton defended his handling of foreign affairs and the two-day summit that brought Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein to Washington. "Those leaders promised me they would not quit until they resolved the issues," Clinton said.
The two presidential candidates clashed over most of the world's hot topics, including:
-- Bosnia: Clinton claimed credit for peace in Bosnia and noted recent elections there; Dole said U.S. troops were to have left Bosnia in a year, but now their stay has been extended.

-- Somalia: Dole said Americans were "dragged through the streets" for a mission that expanded beyond humanitarian concerns and into nation-building; Clinton said he took full responsibility for the events, stressing that U.S. troops were under a U.S. commander, not the United Nations.

-- Haiti: Clinton said that Haiti was governed by a dictator when he took office but now is headed by a democratically elected president; Dole said Haiti had cost $3 billion and that the Haitian president recently called for protection when he "found out there were death squads on his own property."

-- North Korea: Dole questioned the Clinton administration's plan to provide nuclear technology for power generation to North Korea as a disincentive to their building a nuclear weapons capability, saying that without inspections, "we don't know what's going to happen;" Clinton said, "We've worked hard to end the North Korean nuclear threat."

-- Cuba: Dole said Clinton should send a stronger signal to Cuban President Fidel Castro over the Helms-Burton law that lets the United States sue foreign firms doing business with Cuba; Clinton said he had toughened the U.S. embargo on Cuba and increased people-to-people contacts as had been favoured by Cuban-Americans.

-- United Nations: Dole faulted Clinton's deployment of peacekeeping troops under U.N. auspices, saying the U.S. president should be the one to send U.S. troops into harm's way; Clinton said U.S. peacekeeping deployments had been successful in Haiti, Bosnia and Kuwait.
